goals: Mechanistic: quantify precipitation partitioning into surface runoff, ET, and sub-surface drainage/recharge across the watershed's elevation and soil heterogeneity
Validation: test partitioning-relevant states against in-domain observations (SWE, WTD) and honestly flag what cannot be validated (streamflow, ET)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM natively resolves the full water balance (ET, runoff, drainage, snow, per-layer soil moisture) at each sampled point; NLDAS-2 supplies elevation-resolved forcing across the 1625 m relief, making elevation a genuinely testable axis here.

answerable: Per-column partitioning of P into ET, surface runoff, and sub-surface drainage/recharge
Soil-texture control on partitioning (SSURGO per column)
Elevation/climate control on partitioning through NLDAS orographic precip/temperature and simulated snow (with sub-12 km terrain unresolved)
Water-table depth validation against USGS wells (co-located, with expected 1-D vs lateral-flow drift)

not_answerable.aspect: Validation of runoff via basin/gauge streamflow
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral routing or column-to-column exchange, so there is no native integrated streamflow to compare against the 93 USGS gauges
No flux towers in-domain (observations_missing) — ET can only be checked against literature/analog, not co-located

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km (ridgeline) elevation effect on snow/precip
not_answerable.why: NLDAS nearest 12 km cell has no within-cell lapse rate; ridgetop SWE will be underestimated

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soil classes) with targeted oversampling
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands x ~3 dominant soil classes ~= 12 columns spans the two resolvable drivers with one representative column per realized band-soil combination; smallest set that separates elevation/snow effects from soil effects on partitioning without a blind dense grid.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate extra columns in the rain-snow transition (1150-1550 m), where melt timing most strongly controls the runoff/recharge/ET split, and in valley-bottom/riparian corridors where recharge and soil-moisture-water-table exchange are strongest; place high-band columns near SNOTEL sites to link the elevation signal to SWE validation.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light replication (1 extra column) in the rain-snow transition band to capture soil variability where partitioning is most sensitive.

sampling_plan.reason: Warmest/driest, ET- and infiltration-dominated; anchors the low end of the elevation partitioning gradient and overlaps USGS wells for WTD validation.
Transitional climate/soil combination; separates soil-texture control from elevation control on runoff vs recharge.
Most sensitive zone where melt timing governs the runoff/recharge/ET split; oversampled across soil classes to resolve partitioning sensitivity.
Snow-dominated end-member; co-located with SNOTEL to validate SWE that drives the elevation partitioning signal.

sampling_plan.group: validation columns pinned to SNOTEL sites
sampling_plan.reason: Co-located with the 6 SNOTEL stations for direct peak-SWE comparison; count fixed by station availability.

sampling_plan.group: validation columns pinned to USGS wells
sampling_plan.n: unknown - depends on well density in-domain
sampling_plan.reason: Co-located with available USGS wells for WTD validation; count dictated by data, not design.

validation_design.comparison: co-located - nearest column to each station; expect ridgetop underestimation from 12 km cell averaging
validation_design.metric: bias and RMSE on peak SWE and melt-out date

validation_design.comparison: co-located where wells fall near columns; 1-D equilibrium expected to differ from lateral-flow equilibrium (drift is itself a result)
NOT co-locatable - single-column ELM produces no integrated streamflow; would require routing/aggregation of columns to a gauge's contributing area
analog only - no in-domain towers; compare against literature/regional analog ET, clearly labelled non-co-located

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 baseline forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.why: Recharge and water-table targets are meaningless from cold-start default ~8.8 m; warm start scales across the watershed
Single-column ELM has no lateral transport, so per-column runoff cannot be compared to integrated gauge streamflow
requires_capabilities.blocks: validation of runoff against the 93 USGS gauges

requires_capabilities.why: No flux towers in-domain; ET partitioning cannot be co-located-validated
NLDAS 12 km cell averages over terrain, underestimating ridgetop SWE and within-cell precip gradients

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM + SSURGO raster sampling and HUC8 boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: Deterministic expander needs these to turn the stratified rules into concrete columns
requires_capabilities.blocks: conversion of strategy to placed columns

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL and USGS well observation ingest
requires_capabilities.why: Needed to pin and score co-located SWE and WTD validation

assumptions: Naches is within CONUS so NLDAS-2 elevation-resolved forcing applies (no Qian T62 fallback).
SSURGO provides at least ~3 distinct dominant soil textures across the sampled bands; realized band-soil combinations may be fewer than 12.
USGS well records exist at usable depth/frequency within or near the domain; count unknown until data density is checked.
Multi-year forcing windows and adequate spin-up (or warm start) are budgeted, since recharge/WTD targets require it (NLDAS ~10x Qian cost).
Baseline treatment uses native SSURGO soil and NLDAS baseline forcing; a wet-vs-dry forcing-period contrast is a possible secondary sensitivity, not the primary run.
open_questions: How many USGS wells fall within/near the domain with reliable WTD records, and at what depths?
Should we run a wet-year vs dry-year forcing contrast to bound interannual partitioning variability, or fix a single representative multi-year window?
Is basin-integrated runoff validation a priority? If so, routing/aggregation must be prioritized in the backlog.
Preferred spin-up approach: WTD-informed warm start (recommended, scalable) vs multi-year cold spin-up?
